question: A support-ticket agent receives a simple, fully answerable question. On the very first request, Claude's response has stop_reason "end_turn" and contains only a text answer, with no tool_use block at all. An engineer flags this as a bug, assuming every task must go through at least one tool call before the loop can end. Is this assumption correct?
options: A) Yes, because the API rejects any first response carrying stop_reason "end_turn" and requires the client to resend the request
B) Yes, the loop must always force at least one tool_use round trip before accepting stop_reason "end_turn" as genuine completion
C) No, but only because the Messages API silently inserts a placeholder tool_use block whenever no real tool call was necessary
D) No, stop_reason "end_turn" on the first response is a valid immediate completion whenever Claude can answer without needing any tool
correct_answers: D) No, stop_reason "end_turn" on the first response is a valid immediate completion whenever Claude can answer without needing any tool
explanations: Incorrect. The API does not reject first responses carrying stop_reason "end_turn"; ending on the very first turn is an entirely normal outcome.
Incorrect. Forcing an unnecessary tool call before accepting completion is itself an anti-pattern; not every task needs a tool, and the loop should trust stop_reason as given.
Incorrect. The API does not insert placeholder tool_use blocks; a response with no tool_use block simply means no tool was requested.
Correct. There is no requirement that a task pass through a tool call; if Claude can answer directly, stop_reason "end_turn" on the very first response is a legitimate, complete result.
